jobs.plain: Creating new soups and stews for supermarkets
jobs.title: Development Chef
jobs.short: Little Pantry Kitchen makes fresh soups for supermarkets. A development chef invents new recipes, tests them in a small kitchen, and then works out how to make the same thing in huge pots. You’d also present new products to the supermarkets’ buyers.
week: create
Come up with new soups and stews and cook the first versions
hands
Turn a 5-litre recipe into one that works in a 2,000-litre pot
write
Write each recipe down exactly, with what it costs to make
people
Serve new products to supermarket buyers at tastings
write
Keep up with food trends and what other brands bring out
hands
Cook trial batches in the test kitchen
words: NPD
New product development: the team that creates new products.
customer briefs
A written request from a supermarket, for example: a spicy lentil soup that sells for under £2.
kitchen trials
Test batches, cooked to see whether a recipe works.
scale recipes up
Change a recipe so it works in much larger amounts. Spices and cooking times rarely just multiply.
recipe specifications
The exact recipe, written so that anyone in the factory makes it the same way.
costings
Working out what one portion costs to make.
contract catering
Cooking for offices, hospitals or schools, for a company that runs their kitchens.
allergen labelling
Listing on the pack which allergens the food contains, as the law requires.

asks.wrote: A professional cooking background is essential
asks.why: Your six years in restaurant kitchens are exactly this.

asks.wrote: Degree in Food Science or Culinary Arts preferred
asks.why: They would like it, and they will look at people without it.

asks.wrote: Knowledge of food costing and allergen labelling
asks.why: No softening word, so it counts as a must. A food factory does both in more detail than most kitchens.

asks.wrote: Experience in food manufacturing would be a bonus
asks.why: Nice for them, not needed to apply.

asks.wrote: Passion for food and a creative mindset
asks.why: Nobody can measure this. It describes the person they imagine.

know: Of the three jobs, this one is the closest to cooking.
The team is small: four people.

jobs.plain: Checking that a food factory makes safe food
jobs.title: Quality Assistant – Food Production
jobs.short: Example Foods makes ready meals for supermarkets. Every day, someone has to check that the food is made safely and that the records prove it. You’d do those checks, take samples, and help find out what went wrong when a customer complains.
week: check
Walk the production lines and check that hygiene rules are followed
check
Check the records the line teams fill in, such as cooking temperatures
data
Take samples of products and note down the results
write
Look into customer complaints and write down what went wrong
people
Explain the quality rules to the people working on the lines
org
Help get ready for visits from supermarket inspectors
words: Technical team
In food factories, the team that looks after safety and quality. It has nothing to do with machines or computers.
HACCP
Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points: a system for finding the points where food could become unsafe, and checking them.
CCP
Critical control point: one of those points, such as the cooking temperature of a pie.
foreign body
Anything in the food that shouldn’t be there, such as plastic, metal or a hair.
root cause analysis
Finding the real reason something went wrong, not just the first one you see.
BRCGS
A food safety standard that UK supermarkets usually expect their suppliers to meet. Factories are checked against it regularly.

asks.wrote: Level 3 Food Safety qualification is essential
asks.why: A must. Many chefs have Level 2. Level 3 is a short course, and it is worth asking whether they would pay for it.

asks.wrote: Experience in a food environment (manufacturing, catering or retail) is essential
asks.why: Six years in restaurant kitchens counts as catering.

asks.wrote: HACCP Level 3 is desirable, or a willingness to complete it
asks.why: A wish, and they offer a way in: being willing to do the course is enough.

asks.wrote: Good attention to detail and confident using Excel
asks.why: No softening word, so a must. Confident here means everyday lists and tables, not complicated formulas.
Nobody can measure this, so don’t count it against yourself.

know: The hours are daytime, Monday to Friday, and the ad says so clearly.
The factory supplies supermarkets, so their inspectors visit too.
A free hot meal every shift is included.

jobs.plain: Buying fresh fruit and vegetables for a food supplier
jobs.title: Assistant Buyer – Fresh Produce
facts: 3 days a week in the office
jobs.short: Harbour & Hill delivers fresh food to restaurants, cafés and schools. Someone has to decide what to buy from farms and traders each day, and at what price. You would help the main buyer do that, and keep an eye on which suppliers are reliable.
week: org
Place the day’s orders with farms and traders
data
Keep track of which suppliers deliver on time and at the right price
data
Watch how prices change and help argue for better ones
people
Call suppliers when something goes wrong
check
Keep product details correct in the ordering system
people
Work with the warehouse and sales teams
words: Foodservice
Selling food to restaurants, cafés, schools and hospitals, rather than to shoppers.
fresh produce lines
Products. Each item they sell, like a box of lemons, is one line.
growers and wholesalers
Farms, and the traders who buy from farms and sell on.
sales forecasts
Estimates of how much will sell next week, based on past weeks.
supplier performance
How reliable a supplier is: on time, good quality, the agreed price.
procurement
Another word for buying, used by bigger companies.
seasonality
Knowing what grows when, and how that changes price and quality.
VLOOKUP and pivot tables
Two Excel features for finding and summing things up in long lists.
hybrid
Some days in the office, some at home.

asks.wrote: A strong understanding of fresh produce and seasonality
asks.why: No softening word, so a must. This is knowledge about food, not about offices.

asks.wrote: Strong numeracy and good Excel skills
asks.why: A must. In the same line, two Excel features are only “a plus”, so one line holds a must and a wish.

asks.wrote: Previous buying or procurement experience is an advantage but not required
asks.signal: is an advantage but not required
asks.why: A wish, and they say so twice. Ordering stock from suppliers in a kitchen is buying on a small scale.

asks.wrote: A full UK driving licence would be nice to have
asks.why: Only for the odd visit to a supplier.

asks.wrote: Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment
asks.why: Hard to measure. It means several things happen at once.

know: It’s a desk job with lots of calls, three days a week in the office.
The ad says buying experience is not required, in so many words.
